task.description:
Design the fix for LUA-08 (instruction limit), LUA-09 (memory limit), LUA-10 (wall-clock timeout) -- SCOPE NARROWED per human-operator-confirmed decision: GH-495/ISS-0169 originally covered 9 requirements (LUA-08..16); this run now covers ONLY the 3 limiters, since they are self-contained and share one hook installation. The remaining 6 requirements (LUA-11/13 and LUA-12/15/16) have been split into their own new issues -- ISS-0624/GH-591 and ISS-0625/GH-592 -- for future runs. Do NOT expand this design back to cover them.

ISSUE-FIXER's full gap assessment (Step 1, handoff b322f411) confirmed via direct source reading: all three limiter modules (instruction_limiter.zig, memory_limiter.zig, timeout.zig) compile and their core logic is correct in isolation, but NONE are wired into createSandboxedState/executeSource -- executor.zig has ZERO call sites for installHook, MemoryLimiter.alloc, or TimeoutContext outside test pins. This is genuine, documented, honest debt (the source files' own header comments say so explicitly). A test added during GH-500 calls installHook/MemoryLimiter.alloc for real but only proves they execute without crashing -- it does NOT prove actual termination/rejection, since it never drives a script through lua_pcall with a limiter installed.

SPECIFIC FINDINGS TO DESIGN AROUND:
1. LUA-08: installHook() currently stores its limiter pointer via a SCRIPT-WRITABLE Lua global (__limiter__ set via lua_setglobal) -- the same forgery class __limiter__/host_context.zig's REGISTRY_KEY pattern was built to close for capabilities. This must move to LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, reusing host_context.zig's established pattern, not the vulnerable global-based one.
2. LUA-08's max_instructions currently only has a source via executeScriptWithManifest's manifest -- the plain executeScript path (no manifest) has no limit source at all. Design must specify what happens for unmanifested execution (a default limit? no limit, documented as intentional? -- make and justify this decision).
3. LUA-09: MemoryLimiter.alloc() is never passed to lua_newstate (which always uses defaultAlloc, unbounded) -- design how createSandboxedState threads a configurable max_memory_bytes through and switches the allocator.
4. LUA-10: pure host-side timeout-checking cannot interrupt a tight Lua loop by itself (per src/design/lua-integration.md section 15's own honest assessment) -- the practical mechanism is folding TimeoutContext.checkTimeout() into the SAME LUA_MASKCOUNT hook callback LUA-08 installs (check elapsed wall-clock every N instructions, not just instruction count), so LUA-08 and LUA-10 share ONE hook installation. Design this combined hook precisely.
5. Each requirement needs a test proving the REAL failure mode: LUA-08 needs a runaway `while true do end` script actually terminated within a bounded budget (not merely that installHook can be called); LUA-09 needs a script allocating past a deliberately tiny cap actually rejected as a script failure; LUA-10 needs a runaway loop interrupted by ELAPSED TIME specifically (isolated from LUA-08's instruction-count trigger, e.g. a high/no instruction limit but a short timeout) -- these must be genuinely mutation-checkable, not just 'the function was called'.
acceptance_criteria: installHook uses LUA_REGISTRYINDEX for its limiter pointer, not a script-writable global -- matching host_context.zig pattern
max_instructions source decided and justified for both executeScript (no manifest) and executeScriptWithManifest paths
createSandboxedState threads a configurable max_memory_bytes and switches lua_newstate to use MemoryLimiter.alloc
LUA-08 and LUA-10 share one combined hook installation checking both instruction count and elapsed wall-clock

Three genuinely mutation-checkable tests designed: LUA-08 proves actual termination of a runaway script, LUA-09 proves actual allocation rejection, LUA-10 proves interruption by elapsed time isolated from instruction count
No implementation code beyond illustrative Type E signatures
Design explicitly does not expand scope to LUA-11/12/13/15/16 (deferred to ISS-0624/ISS-0625)

result.summary: Designed the wiring of LUA-08 (instruction limit), LUA-09 (memory limit), and LUA-10 (wall-clock timeout) into src/lua/executor.zig's createSandboxedState/executeSource. Key decisions: (1) moved the instruction limiter's pointer storage from the script-writable __limiter__ global to LUA_REGISTRYINDEX under a private key, mirroring host_context.zig's installContext/contextFromState pattern exactly (lua_pushlightuserdata + lua_setfield to install, lua_getfield + lua_type guard + lua_touserdata + lua_pop to read, null on any doubt); (2) LUA-08 and LUA-10 share a single combined LUA_MASKCOUNT hook callback (lua_sethook accepts only one callback per state) that checks both instruction count and TimeoutContext.checkTimeout() every 100 instructions -- this is the only mechanism in this codebase that can interrupt a tight `while true do end` loop, since it contains no host call for a separate watchdog to intercept; the two trip conditions are distinguished by error-message text but not by a new typed field (kept additive to the existing error taxonomy); (3) executeScript (no manifest) now uses a documented conservative default (manifest.Limits' MIN_INSTRUCTIONS/MIN_MEMORY_BYTES/MIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) rather than being left unlimited, because leaving it unenforced would make the unmanifested path a strictly weaker sandbox than the manifested path for no documented reason, contradicting executeScript's own doc comment that it must never become a way to bypass a gate; (4) MemoryLimiter.alloc is wired as lua_newstate's allocator function (replacing defaultAlloc) with max_memory_bytes threaded through a new internal RunLimits struct shared by both entry points. Specified three mutation-checkable tests: TC-LUA-08-01 (while-true-do-end terminated within a small instruction budget, isolated from timeout via a generous timeout_seconds, asserting error-message content and a hang under the pre-fix wiring), TC-LUA-09-01 (a large-table-building loop rejected under a tiny memory cap, isolated from instruction/timeout limits, asserting peak memory never exceeds the cap and that reverting to defaultAlloc makes the same script succeed), TC-LUA-10-01 (while-true-do-end interrupted by elapsed time specifically, isolated from instruction count via max_instructions=10,000,000 and timeout_seconds=1, asserting the TimeoutContext.timed_out flag and a materially different wall-clock outcome if the timeout branch is removed). Explicitly out-of-scope section confirms no design changes reach LUA-11/12/13/15/16 (ISS-0624/GH-591, ISS-0625/GH-592). Lint passed: BLOCKER=0 MAJOR=0 MINOR=0.
